why: Slack paid time from falling workload is not one of the six planted problems. The truth backs the finding's main claim. In every year 2016-2025, clocked hours run 1.006-1.008 times the true operation hours (t404), so the clocked figures are honest. True work fell from 121,721 h (2016) and 117,890 h (2017) to 106,265 h (2025) while paid hours held, so the growing unclocked time is real idle capacity. The 2016 drop is real: true/estimate fell within the year (laser 0.989 to 0.807, brake 1.057 to 0.855, Jan to Dec) while clocked/true stayed about 1.00-1.01 (t405). That settles the booking-versus-efficiency question the analyst left open: it was efficiency, not a booking change.
